rows.q: How long is the waiting period for flood insurance?
rows.answer:
Flood insurance from the NFIP usually has a 30-day waiting period [1]. If you buy a policy today (2026-10-11), coverage generally starts 2026-11-10; until then you have no flood coverage. That is before hurricane season ends (2026-11-30). Buy before a storm is forecast.
Not official guidance. In dan

rows.q: How many flood insurance claims were there in ZIP 77096?
rows.answer:
ZIP 77096 has 6482 NFIP flood insurance claims on record, 2610 of them since 2017 [1]. 4537 flood policies are in force there. The most claims were in 2017 (2550).
Claims show past flooding in the ZIP, not your exact street; few claims does not mean safe.
Not official guidance. In danger, call 911.

rows.q: How do I avoid contractor scams after a flood?
rows.answer:
To avoid contractor scams after a flood, do not pay a contractor in full upfront or in cash, and always get the offer in writing [1]. Be aware that some contractors may take upfront payment and then fail to do the work [1]. You can report suspected fraud or price gouging to (800) 621-0508 [1].

rows.q: I'm a renter and my landlord never told me the apartment flooded before. What are my rights, and should I buy flood insurance before hurricane season?
rows.answer:
Neither the city nor the county requires flood-risk disclosure to renters, and the only warning is a plat note [1]. You should ask your landlord about past flooding in writing and consider getting renters insurance with a separate flood policy [1].
